author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Sian Heder’s “Being Heumann” opened the Toronto International Film Festival with a dramatization of disability-rights activist Judy Heumann’s campaign to force implementation of Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act. Ruth Madeley plays Heumann, while Mark Ruffalo portrays Joseph Califano, the federal official pressed to sign the regulations.

The film centers on the 1977 occupation of a federal building in San Francisco. Protesters remained for 26 days, demanding enforcement of protections against disability discrimination in federally funded programs. The action became a defining event in the U.S. disability-rights movement.

Most of the cast members are disabled, an approach consistent with Heder’s focus on bringing people often left outside mainstream storytelling into view. Heder won the 2022 Academy Award for adapted screenplay for “CODA,” which also featured deaf performers in central roles.

The Toronto opening gives the new film a prominent festival launch ahead of its public release. “Being Heumann” is scheduled to reach select theaters on November 6 and Apple TV one week later. The production turns a policy fight into a character-driven account of organizing, endurance and the practical consequences of laws that exist on paper but still require implementation.
dek: The drama revisits disability-rights activist Judy Heumann’s leadership in the 1977 Section 504 protest, with a cast led by Ruth Madeley and Mark Ruffalo.
headline: Sian Heder’s ‘Being Heumann’ opens Toronto film festival
